blocking.title: Close reconcile auto-closes tasks imported from issues that were already closed, including restarted ones (reopen loops)
blocking.evidence: toReconcile selects every todo with sourceKind 'github-issue' outside done/closed/review (lines 504-514, CLOSE_RECONCILE_SKIPPED line 77). It does not check whether the poller imported the task or whether the issue was open at import. reconcileClosed (lines 386-430) calls transitionTodos(deps, teamId, [t.id], 'closed', ISSUE_INTAKE_ACTOR) as soon as githubIssueState reports closed (line 423). transitionTodos then runs stopActiveStepsAfterExit (chief-tools.ts). importGithubIssue accepts closed issues: projectIssue allows state 'closed' and no state check exists. The web import dialog offers the filter on purpose: apps/web/src/pages/github-issues-dialog.tsx STATE_FILTERS { id: 'closed', label: '已关闭' }. Ticket #1406 scopes this rule to issues the poller took ('被领的 issue 在 GitHub 上关了：对账收尾为 closed'). No test in issue-intake.test.ts covers a task imported from an issue that was already closed.
blocking.failurePath: PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE=1 and the team has a GitHub connection. A user opens the project's import dialog, picks the 已关闭 filter, imports closed issue #N and starts the task (phase todo, then queued/planning/building). On the next sweep (at most 5 minutes later), toReconcile contains it, githubIssueState returns state 'closed', the re-read phase matches, and transitionTodos closes the task and stops its active steps. Importing again returns 409 because sourceRef is kept. Reopening (closed to todo) is undone on the following sweep. With intake on, work started from a closed issue cannot be kept alive, which breaks an existing import path. Possible fixes: limit the reconcile to tasks whose issue was open at import (for example, record that, or only act on an open-to-closed change this process observed), or limit it to tasks the poller imported.
skeptics:
I traced the failure at f9114471 and it is real.

1. Closed issues can be imported by hand. The web dialog apps/web/src/pages/github-issues-dialog.tsx offers STATE_FILTERS 'closed' (已关闭) and 'all'. Clicking a row calls importGithubIssue. The route is routes-projects.ts:142-143 and its body is only {number}. importGithubIssue (github-issues.ts:128-173) never checks issue state. createTodo writes sourceKind 'github-issue' and phase 'todo'.

2. The close reconcile cannot tell these tasks apart. issue-intake.ts:504-514 selects every todo with sourceKind 'github-issue', a non-null sourceRef, and phase not in CLOSE_RECONCILE_SKIPPED = ['done','closed','review']. Nothing records whether the poller imported the task or whether the issue was open at import. The teamIds set also includes teams that only have such todos (lines 515-518).

3. The task gets closed. reconcileClosed (lines 386-430) reads githubIssueState. If the state is 'closed', it re-reads the phase, which is unchanged, and calls transitionTodos(deps, teamId, [t.id], 'closed', ISSUE_INTAKE_ACTOR). phase.ts allows todo, queued, planning, confirm, building and failed to go to closed. transitionTodos (chief-tools.ts:1051-1061) then runs stopActiveStepsAfterExit, so active steps are stopped as well. The task does not even have to be started: the PR's own test 11 '…todo / failed 卡同样关闭' asserts that a todo-phase card on a closed issue is closed.

4. Reopening loops. After the task closes, the next sweep leaves it out of toReconcile and drops its stateCache entry (lines 431-433). A reopen (closed to todo, the only edge out of closed) puts it back in toReconcile. A fresh 200 read returns 'closed', so the task is closed again. Importing the issue again returns 409, because the closed task keeps its sourceRef (github-issues.ts:139).

All of this needs PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE=1 and a team GitHub token; the loop is opt-in. Ticket #1406 scopes the rule to issues the poller took ('被领的 issue 在 GitHub 上关了'). The code applies it to every github-issue task, and no test covers a task imported from an issue that was already closed.

I confirmed the failure at f9114471. Path:
(1) The import dialog lets a user pick closed issues: apps/web/src/pages/github-issues-dialog.tsx has STATE_FILTERS { id: 'closed', label: '已关闭' }.
(2) POST /api/projects/:id/github/issues/import (routes-projects.ts:140-145) calls importGithubIssue. That function (github-issues.ts:128-173) only checks sourceRef claims and never checks the issue's state. createTodo inserts the task with phase 'todo', sourceKind 'github-issue' and sourceRef github:o/r#N (todos.ts:338).
(3) With PACMAN_ISSUE_INTAKE on, every sweep in issue-intake.ts:504-514 puts every github-issue todo whose phase is not done, closed or review into toReconcile. It does not filter on poller-imported tasks or on the issue being open at import. teamIds includes toReconcile's teams, so reconcileClosed runs whenever the team has a token.
(4) reconcileClosed (386-430) gets state 'closed' from githubIssueState. The fresh phase still equals the phase it read, so it calls transitionTodos(..., 'closed', agent actor). todo, queued, planning, confirm, building and failed can all move to closed (phase.ts PHASE_TRANSITIONS). The agent-actor gate in transitionTodos only blocks done from review or confirm, so the close goes through, and stopActiveStepsAfterExit runs for to === 'closed'.
(5) Reopening (closed to todo) puts the task back into toReconcile. The issue reads closed again, either from a fresh read once the key is pruned or from a cached 304, so the next sweep closes it again: a reopen loop.
(6) The existing test '11 todo / failed 卡同样关闭' asserts that a 'todo' card for a closed issue is closed. No test separates tasks imported from issues that were already closed.
(7) The PR's Risk section does not mention or accept this. The ticket's failure mode is about issues the poller took ('被领的 issue 在 GitHub 上关了').

Result: with intake on, a task imported from a closed issue is closed within about 5 minutes, whether or not it was started, and cannot stay reopened.

suggestions.title: Only the first page (100 oldest) of labeled open issues is read; claimed or ineligible issues there starve newer ones
suggestions.evidence: githubOpenIssuesWithLabel requests state=open&labels=...&sort=created&direction=asc&per_page=100 and never follows Link rel="next". intakeProject (issue-intake.ts lines 292-378) loops only over that page. Two kinds of issue stay in it forever: issues counted as 'claimed' (a done or closed task exists but the issue is still open with the label, such as a segmented ticket like #1406 itself), and 'not-eligible' issues (labeler below triage, or more than 100 events).
suggestions.failurePath: A repository has more than 100 open issues labeled ready-for-agent, and the 100 oldest are all claimed or ineligible. Each sweep reads the same first page (and events for up to 100 issues), and nothing newer is ever imported. The tally shows candidates and claimed counts but no imports. The PR's Risk section does not mention this; README says issues are taken oldest first without that limit. This is not imminent at today's 9 labeled issues.

suggestions.title: A sweep that fails outside the per-team try is swallowed with no log
suggestions.evidence: In sweep() (issue-intake.ts lines 490-541), the project and todo queries and the permission-cache prune sit in try/finally with no catch. The scheduler calls `void issueIntake.sweep().catch(() => {})` (lines 214 and 216), which drops the error. When the sweep throws, the 'issue intake sweep' tally line at line 539 is never reached.
suggestions.failurePath: The initial project or todo select throws (for example SQLITE_BUSY, or a schema mismatch after a migration). Every 5-minute sweep then rejects, the scheduler's empty catch drops the error, and no tally or error line is logged. Intake stops silently while the startup log still says 'github issue intake on'. Logging in the scheduler's catch, as the per-team catch already does, would surface it.

suggestions.title: D5 vets the labeler, not the content: issue body or title edited after labeling is imported and dispatched unreviewed
suggestions.failurePath:
Three facts set up the gap. An outside user can always edit the body and title of an issue they opened. The intake queues labeled issues oldest first behind a 3-per-project cap, so an issue can wait several sweeps or days. The D5 verdict reads only label events.

Trace: an outsider opens a benign issue N. The owner applies ready-for-agent. The outsider then edits the body or title to carry instructions. On a later sweep, labelerVerdict (issue-intake.ts:326) still finds the owner's labeled event and returns eligible. importGithubIssue then reads the current issue (github-issues.ts:149) and stores the edited body as todo.spec (github-issues.ts:163). orchestrateTodo quotes it into the chief's orchestration user message, which the chief treats as the task goal, and the chief dispatches builds with no human at import time.

The written D5 rule is met: labeler checked, body kept out of the system layer. But the injection defense rests on the labeler's review, and this path bypasses it. The README text 'An issue is taken only if the newest labeled event ... was made by a user with triage...' can lead an operator to think the content was vetted.

Options: compare the body's last-edit time with the labeled event and skip the issue when it was edited later (REST does not expose body edits; GraphQL lastEditedAt / userContentEdits does), or require the author to have triage or above. At minimum, state the limit in the README and in the Risk section before the switch is turned on (spec 28 P8).

suggestions.title: Label applied by an app on a user's behalf counts as that user; performed_via_github_app is discarded
suggestions.failurePath:
The PR's own capture (docs/verify/1406/api-notes.txt; fixture events-1406.json) shows ready-for-agent on #1406 was applied with actor xiechimon and performed_via_github_app.slug 'claude'. githubIssueLabelEvents keeps only actor.login (github.ts:552) and drops performed_via_github_app.

Any agent session holding the owner's app-user token or gh login can therefore label an outsider's issue and pass D5. That includes Claude Code lanes and, per ADR 0021 D2, agent machines with a gh login. An imported issue whose body steers its agent into running `gh issue edit M --add-label ready-for-agent` would get issue M imported on a later sweep as if the owner had approved it.

Not a violation of D5 as written. The owner deliberately labels through the claude app, so rejecting app-performed labels would break the current workflow. Consider at least keeping performed_via_github_app in the projection and in the 'candidate taken' log or the task record, so a label applied by an agent can be audited or set apart later.

suggestions.title: Close reconcile acts on every github-issue task of the team, not only intake-taken ones; the issue author can stop active work
suggestions.failurePath:
sweep() selects every todo with sourceKind 'github-issue' outside done/closed/review (issue-intake.ts:504-514). That includes tasks a team member imported by hand through the REST import, and webhook-imported ones, none of which passed D5.

The issue author can always close their own issue, even as an outsider. When they do, githubIssueState returns closed and transitionTodos(..., 'closed') runs (issue-intake.ts:423), which calls stopActiveStepsAfterExit on queued, planning, building, confirm or failed tasks. A non-collaborator's action stops in-flight agent work the team started on their own.

The ticket's failure-mode list does say that a closed issue closes its task (被领的 issue 在 GitHub 上关了 → closed), the phase change is reversible, and the README says 'An imported task'. Consider limiting the reconcile to tasks the intake itself created, or ignoring closes by actors below triage (the issue's closed_by is available on GET issue).
